title: A Manatee Never Runs Out of Teeth Because They Keep Marching

scenes.text: A manatee's teeth get worn flat, and it never runs out.
Its food is full of grit that grinds the enamel down.
So new molars grow in at the back of the jaw.
Slowly they move forward, like a conveyor belt, to replace the worn ones.
When the front molars wear out, they fall away.
Two dozen teeth or more, and the supply never stops.

description:
A manatee's teeth wear flat from gritty seagrass.
New molars grow at the back and slowly march forward to replace them.
What other animal has a feature that never runs out?
first_comment: How long would your teeth last if they wore down every day? Pick the next animal for us.
